Arsch.et:
From Middle High German ars, from Old High German ars, from Proto-West Germanic *ars.
Cognate with Dutch aars, English arse. The alternative neuter gender in the figurative sense probably from a backformation from Arschloch (“arsehole”).

s: Fällt mir natürlich Heiner, das Arsch, wieder ein, weißt du, was der zu mir gesagt hat, als ich ihn auf den Vorfall mit dem Kaffee angesprochen habe?
Reminds me of Heiner, of course, that arse, d’you know what he said to me when I mentioned the coffee incident to him?
Arsch.et:
From Middle High German ars, from Old High German ars, from Proto-West Germanic *ars.
Cognate with Dutch aars, English arse. The alternative neuter gender in the figurative sense probably from a backformation from Arschloch (“arsehole”).

s: Sie hat Feigwarzen um das Arschloch herum.
She's got genital warts around her arsehole.

Arschloch.et: From Middle High German arsloch, from Old High German arsloh. Equivalent to Arsch (“arse, ass”) + Loch (“hole”).

Arschgeweih.et: From Arsch (“arse”) + Geweih (“antler, horns”). Cf. Dutch aarsgewei and English arse antlers.
